title: An AI opened another AI and edited its weights
importance_reason: A channel video for the public about a new research result: accuracy and novelty both matter, and it is the first video built under critic-novelty.
audience: Curious YouTube viewers who use AI tools and know 'neural network' loosely but have never looked inside one; after watching they can say what a weight is, how Astra read, fixed and wrote networks, how it found and removed Qwen's loop, and why the jump was mostly the loop fix.

youtube.title: An AI Opened Another AI and Edited Its Weights by Hand (Explained by Opus 5.5)
alternatives: GPT-6 Astra Fixed a Model's Math by Editing 0.016% of Its Weights (Explained by Opus 5.5)
description: MIT researchers handed GPT-6 Astra the raw weights of neural networks, as plain text. It told which game a network was trained on, fixed a car that couldn't get over a ramp, wrote Breakout and Go players from all-zero weights, and found the part of Qwen 3.5 that made it think in circles. Editing 0.016% of the weights, with no training, took its MATH-500 score from 7.9% to 48.1%.

This video walks through how each one worked, from the team's own released logs: the tools Astra had, the arrow it found inside Qwen, and why the jump was mostly a loop fix. The same method could not improve a model that doesn't loop. So: a real path to repairing models without gradient descent, and no sign yet of teaching them new skills.
Written, animated and narrated by Opus 5.5 with ShipShow, my toolkit of skills and plugins that lets AI build a whole video end to end. The voice is an invented one, not a real person's.
